newsitem.title: USA: US farm deferred payment IRS audits to grow - lawyer.
newsitem.headline: US farm deferred payment IRS audits to grow - lawyer.

text.p: KANSAS CITY, MS., Dec 9 (Reuter ) - The number of U.S. farmers under Internal Revenue Service scrutiny for deferred payment income will grow unless corrective action is taken, a tax attorney told a meeting of the National Grain and Feed Association here on Monday.
"Unless there's a Washington solution, a lot of farmers are going to end up in court over this," said George Benson, tax attorney with McDermott, Will and Emery firm based in Chicago.
The issue at large is the IRS provision called the Alternative Minimum Tax.
A non-binding IRS memo issued on October 4 said that farmers deferring payment for grain could be liable for taxes in the year the actual sale was made under the AMT provision.

Benson said he did not think it was Congress' intention to include deferred farm income when the AMT provision was restructured in 1986. But he said that the provision was arguably "broad enough to include grain sales.
"This is a developing issue that is not going to be resolved overnight," Benson said.
He referred to a pending court case before the U.S. Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals involving an Iowa hog farmer who in 1990 deferred a payment on a hog sale exceeding $900,000 to 1991.
A lower court had ruled the farmer should have included the hog sale in 1990 under the AMT provision.
The decision from the higher court will have broad implications for the entire Agriculture industry, he said.

There's a lot of different ways this (tax issue) could be addressed," said David C. Barrett, counsel for public affairs with the NGFA. Legislation was introduced in the last Congress to address the issue, and the Iowa court decision is also likely to revive legislative interest when Congress reconvenes in January, Barrett said.
